title: SDK assembly lab checklist and playbook notes
body:
Purpose: lightweight, reproducible lab that lets a developer go from code checkout to an instrumented SDK demo in ~20 minutes. Focus is on minimal infra, clear failure modes, and telemetry contract so product/observability teams can validate signals early.

Audience: new eng-devxp hires, rotating SREs helping customers, solutions engineers doing demos. Not a full production runbook — lab-first.

Top-level constraints / goals:
- 20 minute happy path for a working sample app calling Redwood hosted API and local sidecar emulation.
- Telemetry emitted for: request.start, request.end, token.count, fallback.used, latency.ms, error.code.
- Local-first: single docker-compose up to start stubbed Redwood gateway + example app.
- Deterministic example prompts and test vectors for QA.
- Low cognitive load: explicit checklist with verifiable green/red checks.

Essential checklist (lab flow):
1) git clone && cd sdk && ./dev-setup.sh (creates virtualenv, deps, local certs).
2) docker-compose -f docker/local-lab.yml up --build (starts rwrw-sidecar, redis cache stub, telemetry-collector).
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=local-demo-key && ./examples/cli-chat --prompt "Summarize this note" --model rdlite-8b
4) open http://localhost:9001/lab-dashboard to confirm request.start/request.end events.
5) run ./tests/lab-smoke.sh to validate token counts and fallback route.

Common failure modes and quick fixes:
- Sidecar 502 on startup: check local certs (./dev-setup.sh --regen-certs) and increase sidecar memory in docker-compose.
- Missing telemetry events: ensure TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT env var points to http://localhost:9411 and collector is up (docker ps).
- High latency on first request: expected cold KV-cache miss; re-run once to prime cache.

Telemetry contract (minimal):
- request.start {event_id, trace_id, timestamp, route, dev_env:true}
- request.end {event_id, status, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant}
- token.usage {request_id, tokens_user, tokens_assistant}
- fallback.used {request_id, fallback_reason}

Quickstart snippets (for the README):
- dev-setup.sh sample output lines to assert: "ENV READY", "CERTS OK", "DEPS OK"
- docker/local-lab.yml minimal services: sidecar, telemetry-collector, sample-app

Open questions / next iterations:
- Add a guided web-based lab runner that runs the checklist and marks steps green automatically (UX ask).
- Decide whether to include an ephemeral hosted demo account for SEs; security / billing implications.
- Add a small integration that simulates Dedicated routing and shows fallback to smaller model when capacity is constrained.

Notes to self / reminders:
- Sync with infra on default port choices (9411 vs 14268) to avoid collisions with tracing infra.
- Capture a short Loom recording of the 20-minute run to include in onboarding.
- Create a small k6 script for load smoke to demonstrate batching benefits.

References and quick links:
- GH PR to watch: GH:github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482
- Related Jira: RW-2349 (lab infra), RW-2410 (telemetry schema rev), RW-2502 (SE demo account)

Appendix: dev-setup.sh quick checklist (what script does):
- create venv and pip install -r dev-requirements.txt
- generate self-signed certs for sidecar
- create sample local API key in ~/.redwood/keys.json
- start a prepopulated sqlite vector store for examples

Appendix: example smoke test assertions (lab-smoke.sh):
- exit code 0 if: response contains "Summary:" and telemetry shows token.count >= 5 and fallback.used == false
- otherwise print the last 50 lines of sidecar logs and exit non-zero

If you iterate on this doc, please append a short changelog entry at the top and ping #devexp in Slack with the lab tag.
